newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Sri Lanka plans its first coal-fired power plant.
newsitem.headline: Sri Lanka plans its first coal-fired power plant.

text.p: Sri Lanka's first coal-fired power plant will be operational in the northwestern Puttalam district by 2000, the state-owned Daily News said on Monday.

The new plant, with an initial generation capacity of 300 megawatts (MW), will cost $500 million and will be built at Kalpitiya, some 140 km north of capital Colombo, the newspaper quoted officials of the Ceylon Electricity Board (CEB) as saying.
The officials said the generation capacity of the plant would be expanded to 600 MW by 2004 and another 300 MW would be added later.
An earlier plan to build a thermal power plant in eastern Trincomalee was shelved due to environmental problems.
A CEB official told the newspaper that low-sulphur coal for the Puttalalm plant would be imported from South Africa and Australia.
Sri Lanka currently relies mainly on hydro-electric power and diesel generation to meet its electricity requirements.
The island is experiencing a drought for the second successive year. Water levels in reservoirs have fallen to crtical levels, threatening power cuts.
The CEB said last week that water levels in hydropower resevoirs had fallen to 21 percent of capacity because of the failure of the northeast monsoon and the delayed onset of inter-monsoon showers.
The government banned the use of air-conditioners at the weekend, saying this was necessary to conserve electricity and avoid the power cuts of last year.
The CEB has said it plans to reduce dependence on hydropower to about 57 percent, from almost 84 percent, by mid-1997 by building more diesel-generating capacity.
Sri Lanka's total generating capacity is 1,250 MW.
